_comment: The single source of truth for what every task state means. The UI renders this file; no state is special-cased in code. To describe a new state, add an entry here. Unknown states fall back to UNKNOWN.

stations.label: Broker queue
stations.hint: The message is stored by the broker, waiting for a consumer.

stations.label: Reserved by a worker
stations.hint: A worker has taken the message but is not running it yet.

stations.label: Running
stations.hint: A pool process is executing the task.

stations.label: Lost
stations.hint: No worker is known to be holding this task any more.

phases.attention: Needs a human: Celery itself will not report what is wrong.

states.label: Queued
states.summary: Published to the broker; waiting for a worker with a free slot.
states.detail: Celery reports this as PENDING, but PENDING also means "I have never heard of this task id", so 'queued' here is inferred from the task-sent event, which only exists if the publisher sets task_send_sent_event. With worker_prefetch_multiplier=1 a message waits here until a worker slot is free; with a higher multiplier it may instead sit 'reserved' inside a busy worker while others idle.

settings.name: task_send_sent_event
settings.why: Without it the publisher emits no task-sent event and this state is never seen.

settings.name: worker_prefetch_multiplier
settings.why: Decides how many messages a worker reserves in advance.

states.label: Reserved
states.summary: A worker has taken the message but has not started executing it.
states.detail: The broker still counts the message as unacknowledged. With acks_late=False it is acknowledged just before execution begins; with acks_late=True only after the task finishes.

settings.name: task_acks_late
settings.why: When the message is acknowledged: before running (default) or after it finishes.

settings.name: worker_prefetch_multiplier
settings.why: Messages sit in this state when a worker reserves more than it can run.

states.label: Waiting for ETA
states.summary: Received, but not allowed to run until its ETA/countdown.
states.detail: Derived by this monitor: Celery has no SCHEDULED state. This is how retry(countdown=...) and exponential backoff wait: the worker holds the task in memory until the time arrives. On quorum queues, Celery's native delayed delivery holds it in the broker instead.

settings.name: retry_backoff
settings.why: Produces the growing delays you see here.

states.label: Running
states.summary: A pool process is executing the task right now.
states.detail: The task-started event is sent when execution begins. The result-backend STARTED state additionally needs task_track_started. If the worker dies while a task is here: with acks_late=False the message was already acknowledged, so the task is lost; with acks_late=True the broker requeues it.

settings.name: task_track_started
settings.why: Makes the result backend report STARTED instead of PENDING.

settings.name: task_acks_late
settings.why: Decides whether a worker death here loses the task.

states.label: Succeeded
states.detail: The result is stored in the result backend (if one is configured) and, with acks_late=True, the message is acknowledged now.

states.label: Failed
states.summary: The task raised an exception that was not retried.
states.detail: Celery stores the exception. By default the message is still acknowledged on failure (task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout=True), so a failed task is not redelivered. In a chord, a failed header task means the callback never runs.

settings.name: task_acks_on_failure_or_timeout
settings.why: True by default: failures are not redelivered.

states.label: Retrying
states.summary: This attempt ended with a retry; a new message is on its way.
states.detail: Celery publishes a NEW message for the same task id with retries+1 and an ETA of now + countdown. Note: RETRY is not a terminal state in Celery (it is in UNREADY_STATES). The ball goes back to the queue.

states.label: Rejected
states.summary: The worker refused the message (requeue=False): dropped, or dead-lettered.
states.detail: Raised with Reject(requeue=False). If the queue has a dead-letter exchange the broker parks the message in a dead-letter queue; otherwise it is discarded. A rejected task stores no result, so a chord waiting on it is never told. With requeue=True the message goes back to the queue instead (shown as Queued).

settings.name: task_reject_on_worker_lost
settings.why: Requeues (rejects with requeue) when the pool process dies mid-task.

states.label: Revoked
states.summary: Cancelled (control.revoke) or expired before it could run.
states.detail: Sent by revoke, or when a task's expires time passed. If terminated=True the running process was killed with a signal.

states.label: Replaced
states.summary: The task called self.replace(); its id lives on as a different task.
states.detail: Derived by this monitor. Celery emits no terminal event for the original, so it would look stuck in Running forever. We infer REPLACED when the same task id is published again under a different task name. The new task keeps the old id, which is why a task id is not a unique identity.

states.label: Ended silently
states.summary: No terminal event arrived, but the worker says it is no longer executing this task.
states.detail: Derived by this monitor by comparing a worker's heartbeat 'active' count with the tasks we believe are running on it. The usual cause is a task that called self.replace() (or raised Ignore): its work continues in other tasks, which is why a chord whose callback can never run leaves its parent here. A lost event looks the same.

states.label: Worker lost
states.summary: The worker running this task stopped sending heartbeats.
states.detail: Derived by this monitor. A SIGKILL, OOM-kill or lost host emits no event at all, not even worker-offline. What happens next is decided by acks_late: if True and the broker connection dropped, RabbitMQ requeues the message and another worker restarts the task; if False the task is silently lost.

settings.name: task_acks_late
settings.why: Without it a dead worker's task is lost.

settings.name: task_reject_on_worker_lost
settings.why: Covers a pool process dying while its parent worker survives.

states.label: Suspected hung
states.summary: Running much longer than expected; Celery cannot tell a hang from a slow job.
states.detail: Derived by this monitor and only a guess: Celery has no per-task heartbeat. A soft time limit raises an exception inside the task so it can clean up; the hard limit kills the process.

settings.name: task_time_limit
settings.why: Hard limit: kills the pool process.

states.label: Unknown state
states.summary: A state this monitor has no description for.
states.detail: Could be a custom state set with update_state(), or something added by a newer Celery. It is shown generically rather than hidden.
